claim: bandit B310 / ruff S310 / semgrep dynamic-urllib-use-detected: urlopen on a dynamic URL may permit file:// or custom schemes (publisher.py:126,129; insights.py:134,137)
rationale: The scheme is not attacker-reachable. Every URL these two transports receive is built from a module-level https literal: publisher.py:31 API = "https://api.github.com" through _repo_url() at publisher.py:378 (f"{API}/repos/{repository}"), and insights.py:39 API = "https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com/v1beta" through insights.py:202 (f"{API}/properties/{property_id}:runReport"). settings.py:116-119 additionally validates repository to an "owner/name" shape before it reaches the f-string. No caller can supply a whole URL, so no input can change the scheme. The tools flag _Urllib.request's local view, where url is a str parameter, not the dataflow.

claim: bandit B314 / ruff S314 / semgrep use-defused-xml: ET.parse on untrusted XML is vulnerable to XXE (test_marks_archive.py:198, test_store_archive.py:128)
rationale: The input is not untrusted. Both sites parse the file named by the PRESSLESS_ARCHIVE environment variable — the writer's own WordPress export, a local file supplied by the person running the suite, which CLAUDE.md records as personal data deliberately kept out of this repository. Both tests are skipped by default (a pytestmark on the "archive" marker) and never run in CI, so no adversary supplies the path or the bytes. Adding defusedxml would buy a test-only runtime dependency against a threat that does not exist here, which is the opposite of the project's one-runtime-dependency position (CLAUDE.md, Build and test).

claim: vulture: unused variable 'explains' (marks.py:201), unused function 'root_entries' (publisher.py:227), unused method 'handle_starttag' (test_marks.py:67), unused variable 'pytestmark' (test_marks_archive.py:49, test_store_archive.py:66)
rationale: Four distinct reasons, none of them dead code. 'explains' is a declared field of the frozen Mark dataclass and is assigned by all seven rows (marks.py:221-287); PRESS-0004-marks.md:125 specifies it as part of the Mark table's contract for the cheat sheet, which is not yet built. 'root_entries' is public module API specified in PRESS-0009-publisher.md sections 4.4 and 9, consumed by Setup and the Face, neither of which exists yet. 'handle_starttag' is an html.parser.HTMLParser override invoked by parser.feed() at test_marks.py:76, not by name. 'pytestmark' is read by pytest itself, by name, at collection. Vulture cannot see framework dispatch, spec-declared surface, or an unbuilt consumer.

claim: ruff B905: zip() without an explicit strict= parameter (test_store_archive.py:203)
rationale: strict=True would be wrong here and would break the helper. _first_difference(expected, actual) walks the zip to find the first differing character, then handles the unequal-length case deliberately in the lines immediately after the loop (test_store_archive.py:206-210: sorted by len, then reports "identical for N characters, then one ends" with the extra text). The truncation B905 warns about is the intended behaviour and is compensated for; strict=True would raise ValueError on exactly the length mismatch the function exists to describe, turning a diagnostic into a crash.

claim: mypy arg-type / pyright reportArgumentType: re.fullmatch(row.arg, arg) takes str|None (marks.py:375), and float(raw) takes Any|None (insights.py:292)
rationale: Neither can raise at runtime. At marks.py:373 arg is assigned "text[...] if row.arg is not None else None", so the guard "if arg is not None" on line 374 implies row.arg is not None by construction — a correlated-optional pair no type checker narrows across two names. At insights.py:292 raw may be None, and that is deliberate: the int(float(raw)) call sits inside a try whose except at line 293 catches TypeError as well as ValueError and re-raises it as InsightsError, which is the module's contract for a malformed answer from Google. Making raw non-optional first would move the same check earlier without changing any behaviour.

claim: mypy arg-type (14 hits) / pyright reportArgumentType: **dict[str, object] splatted into Settings() and Entry() in test helpers (test_store.py:61, test_publisher.py:62, test_insights.py:142), and str|None passed to Path()/list.append in tests reading an environment variable
rationale: Test-harness shape, not a defect. The three splat sites are override helpers that build a kwargs dict of correct per-field values and splat it into a frozen dataclass; mypy widens the dict's value type to object because the literals are heterogeneous, and reports one error per constructor field. Every call is runtime-correct and the suite passes. The str|None sites (test_marks.py:70,72; test_marks_archive.py:195; test_store_archive.py:126) read os.environ.get("PRESSLESS_ARCHIVE") inside tests that a pytestmark skips unless that variable is set, so the None branch is unreachable where the code runs. Neither cluster is in shipped code.

claim: Lane settings.py tagged the `except OSError: pass` in `_discard` (settings.py:235-236) as `[tool: bandit B110]`, implying bandit should have caught it
rationale: The tool attribution is wrong and does not reproduce. Bandit run at the LOW threshold (`-l`, below the `-ll` the sweep used) over settings.py returns ZERO B110 hits. B110 (try_except_pass) fires on a bare `except:` or `except Exception:` followed by pass, not on a narrowly-typed `except OSError: pass`, which is what this code has. So this is not a finding check-code filtered by its severity threshold and not a gap in the tool set. The underlying observation — that the swallow carries no inline comment saying why, though its docstring gives the rule it serves — stands as a style note against the language standard, and is not tool-decidable. Recorded so a later sweep does not chase a bandit rule that was never going to fire.
